zoe li: quick follow-up on the precision profiles RFC — we need to finalize the runtime <-> model manifest contract. decisions we still need: a) model manifest fields for quant variants b) runtime request API for per-request precision hints c) telemetry/quality hooks d) rollout/migration plan. thoughts?

matt: +1. propose adding a top-level "quant_profiles" array in the model manifest. each entry: id, precision, fallback, max_seq, calibration_url, enabled flag. e.g.
```json
"quant_profiles": [
  {"id":"q_fp8_default","precision":"fp8","fallback":"fp16","max_seq":1024,"calibration_url":"s3://models/calib/fp8_default.json","enabled":false}
]
```

anita: telemetry note — we must emit per-variant quality deltas and sample counts. schema idea: (variant_id, eval_name, metric, delta, sample_count, hashed_input_id). keep samples hashed for privacy. metrics: ppl_delta, exact_match_delta, bad_token_rate. these power our auto-gates.

ryan: runtime API suggestion: keep existing generation API stable. add optional `precision_profile` field in the request body and `x-precision-hint` header. treat it as a hint by default. example body: `{ "prompt":"...", "precision_profile":"q_fp8_default", "strict": false }`. `strict:true` causes an error if profile unavailable.

matt: also add negotiation flow: if profile requested but not served, runtime returns 202 + `negotiation` block with available profiles and suggested fallback, or auto-fallback if client allows. avoids 4xx churn for clients that accept graceful degrading.

perf-bot: perf snapshot: fp8 throughput +2.6x vs fp16 on batching workloads, median tail +5% latency on short seqs, memory -30%. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/quant/fp8/summary (internal).

zoe li: migration ops plan: models opt-in by owners — `quant_profiles` present but `enabled:false` initially. rollout steps: (1) create profile + calib, (2) shadow evals for 2w logging quality deltas, (3) enable in canary mode 1%->10%->50% with quality gates, (4) full enable. need CLI tooling to register profiles and schedule shadow evals.

anita: testing: add a `precision-sanity` stage in model CI that runs a small eval suite and numerical stability tests (esp KV cache, layernorm). require thresholds to pass. also add randomized seeding tests to catch nondeterminism caused by quant kernels.

ryan: longer term: move precision selection into scheduling layer. scheduler should know capacity per-profile (e.g., nodes that support fp8), cost per-token, and latency delta. policy: pick profile that meets latency SLO at lowest cost. that forces runtime to surface profile capacity hints via service discovery.

zoe li: edge cases: function-calling and structured outputs — quant noise can break strict json schema. require `response_validation` hook for canary traffic to run schema checks and roll back if violation rate increases.

matt: fallback shim idea: runtime can emulate a missing profile by running higher precision and tagging logs as if it were the requested profile. useful for early experiments so owners see quality metrics even when fp8 rollout not yet on hardware. label these as `shim_emulated:true` so metrics exclude from production rollouts unless explicitly allowed.

deploy-bot: build 2026.3.47 succeeded: branch=quant-profiles-api, build_id=2026.3.47, artifacts=quant-profiles-api.tar.gz

ryan: suggest model manifest allow per-layer opt-in metadata: `layers_opt_in: [int]` so we can target only parts of the network for 4-bit/8-bit; helps mitigate quality regressions.

zoe li: actionable list: (1) manifest schema PR (matt) (2) telemetry schema + sample exporter (anita) (3) negotiation + status codes spec (ryan) (4) CI `precision-sanity` tests (anita) (5) shim & canary CLI + ops runbook (matt). i'll open follow-ups and assign. thanks all :rocket:
